subject: History
description: Entry to UPSC level facts about Indus/Vedic/Maurya/Gupta

questions.stem: [Clerk / NTPC tier] The INDUS VALLEY CIVILIZATION is also known as the:
questions.explanation: After the site of Harappa (Pakistan's Punjab), excavated by Daya Ram Sahni in 1921. Mohenjo-Daro followed in 1922 (R. D. Banerji).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: [NTPC / CHSL tier] Ashoka the Great embraced Buddhism after the Battle of:
questions.explanation: Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE) is mentioned in Rock Edict XIII where Ashoka expresses remorse for the bloodshed — the turning point to Dhamma.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: [CGL tier] 'ARTHASHASTRA', the classical treatise on statecraft, was authored by:
questions.explanation: Kautilya, also called Chanakya or Vishnugupta, was the chief minister of Chandragupta Maurya. The Arthashastra, found by R. Shamashastry in 1905 (published 1909), covers statecraft, economics, military strategy.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: [CGL / PO Prelims tier] Consider the following statements about the GUPTA AGE. 1. Gupta era began with Chandragupta I's accession, c. 319-320 CE. 2. The decimal place-value system (including zero) and Aryabhata's work on mathematics and astronomy belong to this period. 3. Kalidasa was a court poet of Samudragupta. 4. The Iron Pillar at Mehrauli, inscribed in the name of 'Chandra', is attributed to Chandragupta II. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is likely WRONG — tradition most commonly associates Kalidasa with the court of CHANDRAGUPTA II VIKRAMADITYA (not Samudragupta). Some historians disagree, but the exam answer follows tradition. Other three are correct.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: [UPSC Prelims tier] Match List-I (foreign traveller) with List-II (Indian court visited). A. Megasthenes. B. Fa-Hien. C. Hiuen Tsang. D. Al-Biruni. List-II: 1. Chandragupta Maurya. 2. Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya). 3. Harsha Vardhana. 4. Mahmud of Ghazni.
questions.explanation: Megasthenes — Greek envoy to Chandragupta Maurya's court (c. 302 BCE), wrote 'Indica'. Fa-Hien — Chinese Buddhist pilgrim during Chandragupta II's reign (c. 399-414 CE). Hiuen Tsang — Chinese pilgrim during Harsha's reign (c. 630 CE), studied at Nalanda. Al-Biruni — Persian scholar who came with Mahmud of Ghazni c. 1017 CE, wrote 'Kitab-ul-Hind'.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: [NTPC tier] Which ancient Indian text is considered the OLDEST of the four Vedas?
questions.explanation: Rig Veda — oldest, composed c. 1500-1000 BCE, 10 Mandalas with 1,028 hymns. Order of composition (traditionally): Rig → Sama → Yajur → Atharva. The Atharva Veda was latest + included only after considerable debate.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: [UPSC Prelims tier] The city of PATALIPUTRA (modern Patna) served as the capital of the following dynasties, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Pataliputra served as capital for Mauryas, Shungas, Kanvas, Guptas, Palas (for a period). The Mughals ruled from Delhi/Agra/Fatehpur Sikri/Shahjahanabad — never from Patna. Patna was a provincial capital under Sher Shah Suri and the British.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: [UPSC Prelims / PO Mains tier] The HARAPPAN civilization's decline is attributed to several factors. Which of the following are plausible contributors (as per current archaeological consensus)? 1. Gradual drying up of the Saraswati-Ghaggar river system. 2. Invasion by 'Aryan' hordes (the OLD theory, now largely discredited in its dramatic form). 3. Climate change and weakening monsoons c. 2000-1800 BCE. 4. Internal socio-economic stress and urban decay.
questions.explanation: Modern consensus favours a COMBINATION of climatic shift (weakening monsoons, drying rivers) + internal urban decay. The 'Aryan invasion' theory in its dramatic Wheeler-era form (1947) is no longer accepted; the encounter with Indo-Aryan speakers is now seen as much more gradual and complex. So statement 2 as an invasion theory is NOT part of the current consensus.
